item.title: No Age For Learning: Re-reading Rassundari Devi’s Amar Jibon And The Politics Of Late-life Education
item.description: 'Amar Jibon' disrupts dominant ideologies that link learning to youth and equate education with institutional advantage, thereby introducing a subversive, embodied, and fundamentally feminist pedagogy. The post No Age For Learning: Re-reading Rassundari Devi’s Amar Jibon And The Politics Of Late-life Education appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: Being Genderfluid In Literature And In The World
item.description: Gender-fluid refers to a gender identity or expression which is not fixed but rather changes across any measure of time. The post Being Genderfluid In Literature And In The World appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: Mapping Indian Feminism Through Poetry: From Naidu To Kandasamy
item.description: By tracing the poetry of these four writers within their respective time periods, the evolution of feminist thought in India becomes glaringly visible. The post Mapping Indian Feminism Through Poetry: From Naidu To Kandasamy appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: Finding My Feminist Joy In Having Standards And Not Compromising
item.description: Having freedom and standards isn't rebellion but rather a political stance that is informed by my gender, age, family structure and class. The post Finding My Feminist Joy In Having Standards And Not Compromising appeared first on Feminism in India.
